rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Cathode rays are electromagnetic waves. ✅ They are streams of charged particles — waves are not deflected by E/B fields.  ·  ❌ The cathode-ray properties depend on the gas used. ✅ They are independent of gas and electrode material, which is why the particle is universal.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Statement 1: Definition of The Electron — Discovery & Properties of Cathode Rays  ·  Statement 2: Theorem related to The Electron — Discovery & Properties of Cathode Rays

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** An electron beam passes undeflected through E = 3.4 × 10⁴ V/m and B = 2 × 10⁻³ T. Find its speed. **Solution:** v = E/B = 1.7 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Millikan measured e/m. ✅ He measured e alone; Thomson had already measured e/m.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### Focus of this tab  ·  The discovery of the electron through cathode-ray experiments — the first subatomic particle, and the starting point of every atomic model. (It sits in this unit as the experimental foundation of electronic structure.)

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The electron is ≈1837 times lighter than a hydrogen atom — the lightest known charged particle.  ·  Thomson received the 1906 Nobel Prize; Millikan the 1923 Nobel Prize.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The charge-to-mass ratio of the electron is: → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### The cathode-ray tube experiments  ·  • A gas at low pressure (≈10⁻² atm) in a discharge tube with ≈10 000 V across the electrodes emits rays from the cathode that travel in straight lines (shadow of the Maltese cross), carry momentum (paddle-wheel rotation) and heat the target.  ·  • **Electric field:** the rays bend toward the positive plate → negatively charged.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The Electron — Discovery & Properties of Cathode Rays is based on fundamental principles.  ·  Statement 3: Condition for The Electron — Discovery & Properties of Cathode Rays to be valid  ·  Statement 4: Principle governing The Electron — Discovery & Properties of Cathode Rays

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Statement 5: Corollary or consequence of The Electron — Discovery & Properties of Cathode Rays  ·  List five properties of cathode rays and the conclusion drawn from each.  ·  How did Thomson determine e/m with crossed electric and magnetic fields?

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Describe Millikan's oil-drop experiment and its result.  ·  Why does the identical e/m for different cathode materials prove a universal particle?  ·  Cathode rays travel in straight lines but are deflected by fields — the basis of the old CRT television.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • **Magnetic field:** they bend in the direction expected for negative charges.  ·  • The deflection is independent of the gas and cathode material → the particle is a universal constituent of all matter.  ·  ### Thomson's measurements (1897)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Crossed E and B fields (velocity selector): undeflected when Eq = Bqv → v = E/B. Then switching off B gives the deflection, yielding e/m = 1.76 × 10¹¹ C kg⁻¹ — about 1837 times larger than the hydrogen ion's e/m.…  ·  ### Millikan's oil-drop experiment (1909)  ·  Balancing the electric force against the weight of a charged oil drop gave the charge of a single electron: e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (quantised — all drops carry integer multiples of e). Combined with e/m, the electron mass is m = 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg (0.000549 u).
